title: Why Use ADBC Scanner?
description: Talk to any [ADBC](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/)-capable database from DuckDB using [Apache Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/)'s columnar wire format end-to-end — no row conversions, no driver-specific glue.

sections.title: What is ADBC?
sections.description: [Arrow Database Connectivity](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/) is a database-client API standard from the [Apache Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/) project that moves data as Arrow [columnar batches](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html) all the way from the database engine to your query. Where [ODBC](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/odbc/reference/odbc-overview) and [JDBC](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/tutorial/jdbc/) convert rows on each side of the wire, ADBC keeps the columnar layout end-to-end.

bulletPoints.label: Standard API, many drivers
bulletPoints.description: [Drivers](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/) exist for [SQLite](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/sqlite.html), [PostgreSQL](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/postgresql.html), [Snowflake](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/snowflake.html), [BigQuery](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/bigquery.html), [Flight SQL](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/flight_sql.html), DuckDB itself, and a growing list of others — anywhere data already lives in or near Arrow.

bulletPoints.label: No row-format intermediate
bulletPoints.description: Result batches arrive as Arrow [record batches](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html#format-record-batches) and feed straight into DuckDB's [vectorized executor](https://duckdb.org/2021/06/25/querying-parquet.html#vectorized-execution) without transposition or per-row allocation.

bulletPoints.label: Pluggable driver model
bulletPoints.description: Drivers are loaded as shared libraries (or via lightweight [`manifest.toml`](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/installation.html#manifests) files) at runtime — no recompiling DuckDB to add support for a new database.

sections.title: Two ways to use it
sections.description: The extension exposes the same underlying ADBC machinery through two surfaces — pick by what you're trying to do. Both can be loaded simultaneously and target the same remote database.

bulletPoints.label: Catalog mode — `ATTACH ... (TYPE adbc, driver '…')`
bulletPoints.description: Mounts the remote database as a DuckDB [catalog](#storage-extensions). Schemas and tables show up under the alias you give `ATTACH`; projection and filter pushdown happen automatically; the driver streams Arrow batches into DuckDB's executor. Read-only — DDL and DML aren't supported through the catalog interface.

bulletPoints.label: Function mode — [`adbc_connect`](#adbc_connect) + scan / execute / insert
bulletPoints.description: Returns a `BIGINT` connection handle you stash in a [SQL variable](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/set_variable). Pass it to [`adbc_scan`](#adbc_scan) / [`adbc_scan_table`](#adbc_scan_table) for arbitrary SELECTs, [`adbc_execute`](#adbc_execute) for DDL/DML, [`adbc_insert`](#adbc_insert) for Arrow-native bulk inserts, and [`adbc_commit`](#adbc_commit) / [`adbc_rollback`](#adbc_rollback) (after [`adbc_set_autocommit`](#adbc_set_autocommit)) for explicit transactions. Close with [`adbc_disconnect`](#adbc_disconnect).

bulletPoints.label: Schema introspection
bulletPoints.description: [`adbc_tables`](#adbc_tables), [`adbc_columns`](#adbc_columns), and [`adbc_schema`](#adbc_schema) expose the remote catalog without running data queries. Useful for dashboards and schema-driven ETL that need to adapt as the upstream changes — and works whether you're in catalog mode, function mode, or both.

sections.title: Driver Setup
sections.description: ADBC drivers ship as shared libraries (`libadbc_driver_*.dylib` / `.so` / `.dll`) plus an optional [`manifest.toml`](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/installation.html#manifests) that names the symbol to load. The extension resolves them in two ways depending on how you reference them in [`adbc_connect`](#adbc_connect).

bulletPoints.label: By name (manifest-resolved)
bulletPoints.description: `'driver': 'sqlite'` looks up a `.toml` manifest in the [standard ADBC search paths](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/installation.html#search-paths). Most install methods — [`pip install adbc-driver-postgresql`](https://pypi.org/project/adbc-driver-postgresql/), Homebrew, system packages — drop manifests in the right place automatically.

bulletPoints.label: By explicit path
bulletPoints.description: `'driver': '/path/to/libadbc_driver_xxx.dylib'` skips manifest resolution — useful for vendored drivers or unusual install locations.

bulletPoints.label: Custom search paths
bulletPoints.description: Pass `'search_paths': '/opt/adbc/drivers'` inside the connect options to add manifest directories without changing OS-level config.

sections.title: ADBC Scanner vs Airport
sections.description: Both extensions stream Arrow over the wire, but they speak different protocols and target different worlds. Use this section to pick the right tool — or load both, since they coexist cleanly.

bulletPoints.label: Use ADBC Scanner
bulletPoints.description: When the system on the other end is a database with an [ADBC driver](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/) — SQLite, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, MySQL, etc. ADBC is a *client API* standard.

bulletPoints.label: Use Airport
bulletPoints.description: When the system on the other end speaks [Arrow Flight](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Flight.html) directly — typically custom services or Flight-native systems like [Dremio](https://www.dremio.com/). Flight is an *RPC protocol*, not a client API. See the [`airport`](/products/extensions/airport) extension.

bulletPoints.label: Both can coexist
bulletPoints.description: Nothing stops you from loading both: ADBC Scanner for traditional databases, [`airport`](/products/extensions/airport) for Flight-native services, all queryable from the same DuckDB session.

useCases.title: Federate live OLTP databases
useCases.description: Run cross-database analytics by pulling tables from PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite into DuckDB on demand — no ETL machinery, no scheduled syncs. Use [`adbc_scan_table`](#adbc_scan_table) for whole tables or [`adbc_scan`](#adbc_scan) for filtered queries.

useCases.title: Bulk-load from cloud warehouses
useCases.description: Scan [Snowflake](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/snowflake.html) or [BigQuery](https://arrow.apache.org/adbc/current/driver/bigquery.html) query results directly into DuckDB for local analysis, joining against Parquet, CSV, or other DuckDB-native sources.

useCases.title: Schema-driven dashboards and ETL
useCases.description: Use [`adbc_tables`](#adbc_tables) / [`adbc_columns`](#adbc_columns) / [`adbc_schema`](#adbc_schema) to introspect remote catalogs and generate dashboards or pipelines that adapt to schema changes without code edits.

useCases.title: Arrow-native bulk export
useCases.description: Push DuckDB query results into a remote ADBC database with [`adbc_insert`](#adbc_insert) — columnar end-to-end, no row-format detour.
